docs.title: Shard Engine
docs.text:
A 3D game engine in C++17 for Windows and Linux. It is split into modules (rendering, physics, audio, input), the whole source is open, and a game is written as a plugin.

Get started Write a game GitHub

docs.title: What it has
docs.text: Area Highlights Rendering OpenGL 4.6 and Vulkan 1.3 backends, render graph, PBR materials, dynamic lights and shadows, probe-based global illumination, reflection probes, baked lightmaps, path-traced reference renders. See Renderer Physics Rigid bodies and collisions with Jolt, stepped at a fixed rate Audio 3D positional audio, reverb zones Input Keyboard, mouse and gamepads, with dead zones and rumble. Input is recorded in replays Assets FBX import (ufbx), compressed and cached textures, JSON serialization generated from reflection Editor ImGui editor with a world tree, gizmos, an inspector, a profiler and hot reload of game code. See Editor Plugins Datapacks without code, native plugins with dependencies, signed packages and registries, and a C ABI that plugins can use with any compiler. See Plugins and modules Simulation Archetype ECS with systems that declare what they read and write. A fixed timestep and seeded random streams make a run deterministic, and it can run without a window or a GPU. See Headless mode and determinism Large worlds 64-bit coordinates and nested reference frames. See Large world

docs.title: Writing a game
docs.text:
A game is a plugin built with the SDK. A script is a class that lives on an actor, like the engine's own scripts, and each source file registers its own scripts, so a game can be as many files as you like.

health.hpphealth.cppmodule.cpp 
#include <shard/game.hpp>

class Health : public Shard::Script {
public:
    // fields: shown in the inspector, saved with the world, each declared where it is
    SHARD_FIELD(float, maxHealth, Range(1.f, 1000.f)) = 100.f;
    SHARD_FIELD(float, current) = 100.f;
    SHARD_FIELD(Shard::Text, label);

    void OnPlay() override { current = maxHealth; }
    void OnTick(float deltaTime) override;
    void Damage(float amount) { current -= amount; }
};

#include "health.hpp"

void Health::OnTick(float)
{
    if (current <= 0.f) Owner().Destroy();
}

// Registers the class
SHARD_REGISTER_SCRIPT(Health)

#include <shard/game.hpp>

// The plugin's entry point, in any one file.
// Every other file registers its own scripts, components and systems.
SHARD_GAME_MODULE()

The tutorial goes through it step by step.

The editor viewport, with probe-based global illumination

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
You need CMake 3.28.2 or later and a C++17 compiler (GCC or Clang on Linux, GCC MinGW on Windows).

git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/Windokk/Shard.git
cd Shard

# Builds the submodules, the engine, the editor and the game module, then starts the editor
./build.sh        # or build.bat on Windows

Fonts, resource folders and Linux packages need a few manual steps : see Getting started.

docs.title: The C ABI
docs.text:
The headers in sdk/include/shard are the contract between a plugin and the engine. This page is generated from their comments, in reading order. See Plugins for the concepts and the tutorial to build a plugin.

Every function says which thread may call it : any, system (from inside a system, possibly in parallel with others), script (from a script callback) or main (the main thread, outside systems). A function returns a ShardResult, either SHARD_OK (0) or a negative error, and the details go to the engine's log under the plugin's id. Strings are ShardStr : UTF-8, not necessarily zero terminated, valid for the duration of the call. A "text out" function takes (buffer, capacity, *size), copies what fits and returns the full length.

Header Interface shard_abi.h base types, versions and rules shard_host.h what a plugin exports and what the host gives it shard_plugin.h shard.plugin 1.2 who the plugin is, as the host read it from the manifest, and where it runs shard_cvars.h shard.cvars 1.0 variables the plugin owns, readable from the console and the config files like the engine's own shard_commands.h shard.commands 1.1 console commands shard_components.h shard.components 1.4 component types described field by field shard_ecs.h shard.ecs 1.1 entities and their components, from inside a system shard_systems.h shard.systems 1.0 functions the engine's scheduler runs every frame, in a phase, in parallel with the systems they do not conflict with shard_events.h shard.events 1.1 events found by NAME, carrying bytes shard_hooks.h shard.hooks 1.0 the points of the engine a plugin can intercept, and cancel shard_services.h shard.services 1.0 interfaces plugins offer each other, by name and version, without including each other's code shard_extensions.h shard.extensions 1.0 what a plugin adds to the engine's subsystems through their extension points shard_content.h shard.content 1.0 the content folders of the loaded modules shard_state.h shard.state 1.0 what a plugin keeps across a hot reload shard_actors.h Interface "shard.actors" 1.2 (1.0 + the fields of a component, one at a time in 1.1 ; stable ids, bounds and neighbours in 1.2) shard_assets.h shard.assets 1.0 the assets of the project, by path and by id shard_audio.h shard.audio 1.0 sounds shard_debug.h shard.debug 1.0 drawing for the developer, in the world, from anywhere : a navigation mesh, the path an agent follows, a field of view, a voxel chunk's bounds, a bone, a network ghost, the node a graph is running shard_editor.h shard.editor 1.2 the editor's windows, menus, toolbar, inspectors and gizmos, drawn with a small set of widgets shard_experimental.h shard.experimental.world_ecs 0.1 the engine's entities from the main thread, outside the systems shard_input.h shard.input 1.1 keyboard, mouse and gamepads, polled ; and the window system's events, in order shard_jobs.h shard.jobs 1.0 the engine's worker threads, for a plugin's own work shard_net.h shard.net 1.0 UDP and TCP sockets, for the networking a game builds itself shard_physics.h shard.physics 1.1 the rigid bodies of actors, ray casts and volume queries, and colliders a plugin builds itself shard_reflect.h shard.reflect 1.0 what exists in the engine and in the other plugins, described at run time ; and functions plugins offer to be called by name shard_render.h shard.render 1.0 what a plugin puts on the screen that the engine's components do not : meshes it builds, textures it fills, sprites, instances and a 2D overlay shard_scripts.h shard.scripts 1.2 scripts, the components that carry a plugin's gameplay code shard_time.h shard.time 1.0 the simulation's clock, and a fingerprint of its state shard_wasm.h Sandboxed plugins (tier 2, "abi": "wasm1") shard_worlds.h shard.worlds 1.1 loading worlds, and prefabs ; and which worlds are loaded

docs.title: shard_abi.h
docs.text:
Shard C ABI : base types, versions and rules. Compiles as C11 and as C++17.

These headers ARE the ABI (see docs/design-notes/c-abi-sdk.fr.md, section 3). The rules :

  • plain C : no classes, references, overloads or enum class; no int, long, bool or size_t inside a struct
  • every struct that crosses the boundary starts with uint32_t structSize; fields are only ever added at the END
  • the host never keeps a pointer it was handed unless the doc of that function says so
  • no exception crosses the boundary; failures are a ShardResult

Changing a struct without bumping SHARD_ABI_MINOR is a bug : tests/plugins/abi_layout_tests.cpp pins every layout.

Value SHARD_ABI_MAJOR 1 SHARD_ABI_MINOR 7

Calling convention of every function pointer in the tables. Empty on x86_64 and arm64.

Value SHARD_CALL SHARD_PLUGIN_EXPORT depends on the platform

Results

typedef int32_t ShardResult;
Value SHARD_OK 0 SHARD_E_INVALID_ARG (-1) SHARD_E_NOT_FOUND (-2) SHARD_E_ALREADY_EXISTS (-3) SHARD_E_WRONG_THREAD (-4) SHARD_E_STALE_HANDLE (-5) SHARD_E_UNSUPPORTED (-6) SHARD_E_OUT_OF_MEMORY (-7) SHARD_E_INTERNAL (-8) SHARD_FALSE 0 SHARD_TRUE 1

docs.title: ShardStr
docs.text:
Strings

UTF-8, not necessarily zero terminated. A string received through a call is valid for that call only : keeping it means copying it.

const char* data;
uint64_t size;

Handles

Never a pointer to a host object. index + generation, so a stale one fails instead of reading freed memory. 0 is never valid.

typedef uint64_t ShardPluginCtx;    // designates a plugin to the host
typedef uint64_t ShardState;    // the reload state being written or read : valid during on_prepare_reload / on_restore only (shard_state.h)

Log levels

Value SHARD_LOG_INFO 0 SHARD_LOG_WARNING 1 SHARD_LOG_ERROR 2

docs.title: shard_host.h
docs.text: Shard C ABI : what a plugin exports and what the host gives it.

docs.title: ShardHostApi
docs.text:
The host's table

One static table for every plugin; a plugin designates itself with the ShardPluginCtx it is handed in each callback. The base is only what is needed to start; everything else is an interface fetched with query_interface, so this table barely grows.

uint32_t structSize;
uint32_t abiMajor, abiMinor;
ShardStr engineVersion;    // "0.9.2", informative

thread : any

void log(ShardPluginCtx ctx, uint32_t level, ShardStr message);

Memory counted against the plugin's budget (manifest budgets.memoryMB). Returns NULL on failure. What is allocated here is freed with free here : never with the plugin's own allocator, and never by the host's.

void* alloc(ShardPluginCtx ctx, uint64_t size, uint64_t align);
void free(ShardPluginCtx ctx, void* p);

Looks an interface up by id ("shard.plugin"). major must match; the interface must be at least minMinor. On success *out points to a struct that starts with uint32_t structSize, valid until the host exits. SHARD_E_NOT_FOUND : the id is unknown, or this host does not offer it (an offline tool has no "shard.systems").

ShardResult query_interface(ShardStr id, uint32_t major, uint32_t minMinor, const void** out);

docs.title: ShardWorldInfo
docs.text:
A world a module is told about. name is valid for the call.

uint32_t structSize;
int32_t assetId;    // the world's asset id in the project, -1 if it has none
ShardStr name;

docs.title: ShardPluginCallbacks
docs.text:
The plugin's callbacks

Same order and meaning as IPlugin. A callback returns SHARD_OK, or an error that makes the host fail the plugin (and the plugins that depend on it) with the message the plugin logged. Every callback is optional : NULL means "nothing to do". All of them run on the main thread.

uint32_t structSize;
ShardResult on_load(void* user, ShardPluginCtx ctx);
ShardResult on_initialize(void* user, ShardPluginCtx ctx);
ShardResult on_enable(void* user, ShardPluginCtx ctx);
ShardResult on_disable(void* user, ShardPluginCtx ctx);
ShardResult on_unload(void* user, ShardPluginCtx ctx);

Hot reload (shard_state.h). on_prepare_reload writes what must survive into state and returns SHARD_OK ; any other result (or no callback) makes the plugin not reloadable. on_restore reads it back in the new binary, after on_enable.

ShardResult on_prepare_reload(void* user, ShardPluginCtx ctx, ShardState state);
ShardResult on_restore(void* user, ShardPluginCtx ctx, ShardState state);

Start and end of every frame while the plugin is enabled. Keep them short : their time is billed to the plugin.

ShardResult on_frame_begin(void* user, ShardPluginCtx ctx, uint64_t frame);
ShardResult on_frame_end(void* user, ShardPluginCtx ctx, uint64_t frame);

Modules : the content folder is mounted (mod://<id>/ is readable, shard_content.h), and what happens to the worlds

ShardResult on_content_mounted(void* user, ShardPluginCtx ctx);
ShardResult on_world_loaded(void* user, ShardPluginCtx ctx, const ShardWorldInfo* world);
ShardResult on_world_unloaded(void* user, ShardPluginCtx ctx, const ShardWorldInfo* world);
ShardResult on_play_start(void* user, ShardPluginCtx ctx, const ShardWorldInfo* world);
ShardResult on_play_stop(void* user, ShardPluginCtx ctx, const ShardWorldInfo* world);

Offline tools : the tool is about to run task ("cook", "bake", "validate") on the project file project. SHARD_OK lets it run ; anything else cancels it, with *message (copied before the call returns) as the reason. Unlike the others, an error here does not fail the plugin.

ShardResult on_tool_task(void* user, ShardPluginCtx ctx, ShardStr task, ShardStr project, ShardStr* message);

Callbacks of later ABI revisions go HERE : the host checks structSize before reading them.

docs.title: ShardPluginInfo
docs.text:
What the plugin fills in its entry point

uint32_t structSize;    // the plugin sets it to sizeof(ShardPluginInfo) of the headers it was built with ; the host reads no field past it
uint32_t abiMajor, abiMinor;    // the plugin sets them to SHARD_ABI_MAJOR / SHARD_ABI_MINOR
ShardStr id;    // informative : the manifest is what the host trusts
void* user;    // handed back to every callback
const ShardPluginCallbacks* callbacks;    // must stay valid until on_unload returned

The entry point of an ABI "c1" plugin (manifest "abi": "c1"). Called once, right after the library is loaded, on the main thread. out is zeroed. Return SHARD_OK, or an error to refuse to load.

typedef ShardResult (*ShardPluginEntryFn)(const ShardHostApi* host, ShardPluginInfo* out);
Value SHARD_PLUGIN_ENTRY_NAME "shard_plugin_entry" 
SHARD_PLUGIN_EXPORT ShardResult shard_plugin_entry(const ShardHostApi* host, ShardPluginInfo* out);

docs.title: ShardRandomState
docs.text:
The state of a PCG32 generator (O'Neill 2014) : state and increment are the two words of Shard's Random class. Whoever holds them continues the sequence with the same code and gets the same numbers on every platform (shard/cpp/random.hpp does).

uint64_t state;
uint64_t increment;

docs.title: ShardPluginApi
docs.text:
uint32_t structSize;

The returned strings stay valid until the plugin is unloaded.

ShardStr id(ShardPluginCtx ctx);    // "com.acme.weather"
ShardStr version(ShardPluginCtx ctx);    // "1.4.2"
ShardStr directory(ShardPluginCtx ctx);    // the plugin's folder, absolute, '/' separators

1.1

The executable the plugin runs in : "editor", "player", "headless" or "tool"

ShardStr host(ShardPluginCtx ctx);

SHARD_TRUE if the manifest asks for that permission ("fs.read:content", "net"...)

int32_t has_permission(ShardPluginCtx ctx, ShardStr permission);

1.2

A generator for the stream name : derived from the run's seed, the plugin's id and the name, so the same name gives the same sequence in a replay of the run, and two plugins never share a stream. Name a stream after what draws from it (an actor's name and the script's), not after the order things started in. The generator is the caller's afterwards : no further call is needed.

ShardResult random_stream(ShardPluginCtx ctx, ShardStr name, ShardRandomState* out);

docs.title: shard_cvars.h
docs.text:
Interface "shard.cvars" 1.0 : variables the plugin owns, readable from the console and the config files like the engine's own. A variable is named "<plugin id>.<name>" by the host. It lives until the plugin is disabled or unloaded ; after that its handle is stale (SHARD_E_STALE_HANDLE). The plugin changes its own variables with set_* (that bypasses the config layers and the read-only flag, as the owner) ; the console and the config files change them from outside. Numeric values are clamped to [min, max].

Value SHARD_IFACE_CVARS "shard.cvars" SHARD_CVAR_READONLY 1u the console and the config files cannot change it 
typedef uint64_t ShardCVar;    // generation << 32 | slot ; 0 is never valid

docs.title: ShardCVarsApi
docs.text:
uint32_t structSize;

thread : main. SHARD_E_ALREADY_EXISTS if the name is taken.

ShardResult create_bool(ShardPluginCtx ctx, ShardStr name, int32_t value, ShardStr help, uint32_t flags, ShardCVar* out);
ShardResult create_int(ShardPluginCtx ctx, ShardStr name, int32_t value, ShardStr help, uint32_t flags, int32_t min, int32_t max, ShardCVar* out);
ShardResult create_float(ShardPluginCtx ctx, ShardStr name, float value, ShardStr help, uint32_t flags, float min, float max, ShardCVar* out);
ShardResult create_string(ShardPluginCtx ctx, ShardStr name, ShardStr value, ShardStr help, uint32_t flags, ShardCVar* out);

thread : any. SHARD_E_INVALID_ARG if the variable is of another type.

ShardResult get_bool(ShardPluginCtx ctx, ShardCVar cvar, int32_t* out);
ShardResult get_int(ShardPluginCtx ctx, ShardCVar cvar, int32_t* out);
ShardResult get_float(ShardPluginCtx ctx, ShardCVar cvar, float* out);

Copies at most capacity bytes (no zero terminator) into buffer and stores the full length in *size : a value longer than the buffer is cut, and the caller can call again with a bigger one. buffer may be NULL to ask for the length.

ShardResult get_string(ShardPluginCtx ctx, ShardCVar cvar, char* buffer, uint64_t capacity, uint64_t* size);

thread : main

ShardResult set_bool(ShardPluginCtx ctx, ShardCVar cvar, int32_t value);
ShardResult set_int(ShardPluginCtx ctx, ShardCVar cvar, int32_t value);
ShardResult set_float(ShardPluginCtx ctx, ShardCVar cvar, float value);
ShardResult set_string(ShardPluginCtx ctx, ShardCVar cvar, ShardStr value);

docs.title: shard_commands.h
docs.text:
Interface "shard.commands" 1.1 : console commands. The command is removed with the plugin (disable or unload). 1.1 added execute: running a command of the console (the engine's, a plugin's) from code -- what a UI button, a graph node or a script does.

Value SHARD_IFACE_COMMANDS "shard.commands"

Runs the command. args are the words after the command name (argCount of them, valid for the call). The callback may point *output to a text to show the user (it is copied before the callback's caller returns : a static buffer or the plugin's own will do). Return SHARD_OK for success ; anything else is shown as a failure, with the output as the message. thread : main

typedef ShardResult (*ShardCommandFn)(void* user, ShardPluginCtx ctx, const ShardStr* args, uint32_t argCount, ShardStr* output);

docs.title: ShardCommandsApi
docs.text:
uint32_t structSize;

The name is used as given : prefix it with your own ("weather.set"). SHARD_E_ALREADY_EXISTS if this plugin already added that name (case does not matter). A name another plugin or the engine already uses is replaced for as long as this plugin lives : the prefix is what keeps commands apart. thread : main

ShardResult add(ShardPluginCtx ctx, ShardStr name, ShardStr help, ShardCommandFn run, void* user);

1.1

Runs a console line ("world.load arena", "render.thread 0") as if it was typed. The command's output is copied as a "text out" : at most capacity bytes into output (may be NULL), the full length in *size (may be NULL). SHARD_OK if the command succeeded, SHARD_E_NOT_FOUND if the line names no command, SHARD_E_INVALID_ARG if it failed (the output says why). A command that changes what the game simulates is the caller's to run from the simulation thread. thread : main

ShardResult execute(ShardPluginCtx ctx, ShardStr line, char* output, uint64_t capacity, uint64_t* size);

docs.title: shard_components.h
docs.text:
Interface "shard.components" 1.4 : component types described field by field.

One registration gives a type two faces, under one name ("<plugin id>.<name>", made by the host) :

  • an ECS component : a block of size bytes on an entity, what systems query and write (shard_ecs.h). Plain data : copied with memcpy, 

    never constructed nor destroyed, so no pointer to memory the plugin owns. What does not fit in the block goes in a blob (1.1, below) ;

  • an actor component : what a world file saves, the editor shows in its inspector and an actor carries. Its fields are the ones described 

    here, read and written at their offset in the block.

An actor that has the actor component has the ECS component on its entity, with the same values : the actor component writes its values to the entity when it is loaded, edited or attached, and reads them back from the entity when the world is saved or copied. So what a system changed is what gets saved. An entity a plugin spawned on its own (shard_ecs.h, cmd_spawn) has no actor : it is not saved.

The type lives as long as the plugin is enabled. Its ECS id stays reserved for the whole run : a plugin enabled again gets the same ShardComponentType back, provided it describes the same size (a type whose size changed needs a restart of the engine).

Blobs (1.1) : bytes the host keeps outside the block, as many as needed (a chunk of voxels), counted against the plugin's memory budget. A field SHARD_FIELD_BLOB holds the ShardBlob handle. The plugin owns its blobs : blob_free gives one back, and all of them go with the plugin (disable, unload). The block is still copied with memcpy, so two blocks may hold the same handle : that is a shared blob, not a copy. The actor component is the exception, it owns the blobs of its blob fields : it saves their bytes with the world (base64), a copy of the actor (play mode) gets copies of them, and removing the component frees them. A system that puts a new blob in such a field frees the one it replaces.

Text and assets (1.2) : a field SHARD_FIELD_STRING holds a ShardBlob too, whose bytes are the UTF-8 text (no terminator) : the actor component owns it like any blob, but the inspector shows it as a text box and the world file saves it as a JSON string. string_set and string_get read and write it without touching the blob by hand. A field SHARD_FIELD_ASSET is an int32_t, the id of an asset of the project (0 : none) : the inspector shows an asset picker, the world file saves the asset by its name, and the engine knows the component uses it.

Life cycle (1.4) : a type may ask to be told when one of its components joins an actor, leaves it, or has a field edited (ShardComponentCallbacks). That is where a plugin makes what the component stands for -- a render object for a chunk of voxels, a navigation agent, a particle emitter's state -- and drops it, without scanning the ECS every frame to find out what appeared.

Value SHARD_IFACE_COMPONENTS "shard.components" 
typedef uint64_t ShardComponentType;    // 0 is never valid
typedef uint64_t ShardBlob;    // 0 is never valid : an empty blob field

Field types : the C type the field has in the block, and how it is saved

Value SHARD_FIELD_F32 1u float SHARD_FIELD_F64 2u double SHARD_FIELD_I32 3u int32_t SHARD_FIELD_U32 4u uint32_t SHARD_FIELD_I64 5u int64_t SHARD_FIELD_U64 6u uint64_t SHARD_FIELD_BOOL 7u uint8_t, 0 or 1 SHARD_FIELD_VEC2 8u float[2] SHARD_FIELD_VEC3 9u float[3] SHARD_FIELD_VEC4 10u float[4] SHARD_FIELD_QUAT 11u float[4] : x, y, z, w SHARD_FIELD_COLOR 12u float[4] : r, g, b, a (the inspector shows a colour picker) SHARD_FIELD_BLOB 13u ShardBlob (uint64_t) : saved as the blob's bytes, not shown by the inspector (1.1) SHARD_FIELD_STRING 14u ShardBlob (uint64_t) holding UTF-8 text : edited in the inspector, saved as text (1.2). 8 per component at most SHARD_FIELD_ASSET 15u int32_t : the id of an asset, 0 for none (1.2) SHARD_FIELD_ACTOR 16u ShardActor (uint64_t) : another actor, saved by its path in the world. Scripts only (1.5)

Field flags. Without any, a field is saved and editable in the inspector.

Value SHARD_FIELD_RUNTIME 1u runtime state : shown by the inspector, read only, not saved SHARD_FIELD_PRIVATE 2u neither shown nor saved : the block keeps it, nothing else sees it (not for a string : use a blob) SHARD_FIELD_ACCESSOR 4u a SHARD_FIELD_STRING of a script that is not a handle : the plugin's own string at that offset, read and writt 
* by the script's text_get and text_set callbacks (shard_scripts.h) instead of a blob (1.5) */ typedef struct ShardFieldDesc { uint32_t structSize;
uint32_t type;    // SHARD_FIELD_*
ShardStr name;    // letters, digits and '_' ; "type", "active" and "tags" are reserved
uint32_t offset;    // in the block, aligned for its type
uint32_t flags;    // SHARD_FIELD_RUNTIME...
float min, max;    // bounds of the inspector's widget ; min == max : none
ShardStr tooltip;    // optional
} ShardFieldDesc;

Told about the actor components of a type (1.4). actor is the ShardActor that carries it, entity its ECS entity, block the component's block (valid for the call). All of them run on the main thread, outside the systems, in the editor's edit mode as well as in play mode, with the values the world file or the inspector gave already in the block.

on_added   : the component became live : its entity exists and its values are in the block. Once per activation (added to an actor that is in
             a world, loaded from a file, copied for the play mode, enabled again after being disabled).
on_removed : it is about to stop being live (removed, disabled, its actor destroyed, the world unloaded) ; the block is still intact. A
             destroyed actor's handle is still valid in this call.
on_changed : a field was edited (the inspector, shard.actors' set_component...) ; `field` is its index in the description's `fields`. A system
             writing the block does NOT call it.

typedef void (*ShardComponentFn)(void* user, ShardPluginCtx ctx, uint64_t actor, uint64_t entity, void* block);
typedef void (*ShardComponentChangedFn)(void* user, ShardPluginCtx ctx, uint64_t actor, uint64_t entity, void* block, uint32_t field);

Value SHARD_COMPONENT_MAX_SIZE 1024u SHARD_COMPONENT_MAX_FIELDS 64u SHARD_COMPONENT_MAX_STRINGS 8u SHARD_FIELD_STRING and SHARD_FIELD_ACTOR fields of one component or script together (1.2)

docs.title: ShardComponentsApi
docs.text:
uint32_t structSize;

Registers a type, from on_load. thread : main. docs.title: shard_ecs.h
docs.text:
Interface "shard.ecs" 1.1 : entities and their components, from inside a system (shard_systems.h).

Every function takes the ShardEcs the system was handed in its ShardSystemCtx : it is valid during that run, on that thread, and nowhere else (SHARD_E_STALE_HANDLE). A system reads and writes only the types it declared (reads / writes of its ShardSystemDesc, SHARD_E_INVALID_ARG otherwise ; an exclusive system may touch anything) : the scheduler relies on these declarations to run systems in parallel, and the result of a frame must not depend on it.

Structural changes (spawn, destroy, add, remove, set_parent) are recorded and applied at the end of the phase, system by system in registration order. spawn returns a placeholder that the later commands of the same run can use ; it means nothing afterwards. Changing the VALUE of a component (through the pointers of each_chunk and get) is immediate.

Moving an actor (1.1) : the engine's own components below are not written through these pointers, the actor's Transform is what drives them. set_local_transform records the new pose ; at the end of the phase the actor's Transform takes it (so does everything that follows a Transform : children, physics, the renderer) and the LocalTransform of the entity then holds it.

docs.title: shard_events.h
docs.text:
Interface "shard.events" 1.1 : events found by NAME, carrying bytes.

The engine's C++ events are found by their C++ type, which a binary built by another compiler cannot name : the C ABI has a channel of its own, where an event is a name ("com.acme.weather.RainStarted") and a payload of bytes whose layout the sender documents. C++ code reaches the same channel (EventRegistrar::SubscribeNamed / EmitNamed). Subscriptions end with the plugin (disable or unload).

Delivery : an event emitted on the main thread outside of the systems is delivered at once, to the subscribers in the order they subscribed. One emitted from a system (any thread) is queued and delivered on the main thread at the end of the frame, the queues of the systems taken in the order of their names : the order does not depend on which system finished first.

docs.text:
Interface "shard.hooks" 1.0 : the points of the engine a plugin can intercept, and cancel. Hooks are found by name ; every one is described by the same struct, whose subject, detail and frame mean what the table below says. Handlers run by priority, then by plugin load order, then in the order they were added : the same order on every run. They are removed with the plugin.

name                 subject             detail          frame
"PreEngineInit"      -                   -               -
"PostEngineInit"     -                   -               -
"PreWorldLoad"       the world's name    -               -       cancellable : the world is not loaded
"PostWorldLoad"      the world's name    -               -
"PrePlay"            -                   -               -       cancellable : play mode does not start
"PostPlay"           -                   -               -
"PreFrame"           -                   -               frame
"PostFrame"          -                   -               frame
"PreSave"            what is saved       -               -       cancellable : nothing is saved
"AssetImported"      the asset's path    -               -
"PlayerConnecting"   the client's name   its address     -       cancellable : the client is refused, `reason` is what it is told
"PreShutdown"        -                   -               -

docs.title: shard_services.h
docs.text:
Interface "shard.services" 1.0 : interfaces plugins offer each other, by name and version, without including each other's code.

A service of the C ABI is a table of function pointers that starts with uint32_t structSize (and, like the ABI's own tables, only grows at its end), plus a self the functions get back. The provider publishes the header of its table ; the users include it. The engine never calls the table : it only hands it out.

A user holds a ShardServiceRef, not the table : resolve it before each use. When the provider is disabled or unloaded, the ref resolves to nothing (SHARD_E_NOT_FOUND) instead of to a table in a library that is gone. Refs are released with the plugin that took them.

docs.text:
Interface "shard.actors" 1.2 (1.0 + the fields of a component, one at a time in 1.1 ; stable ids, bounds and neighbours in 1.2) : the actors of a world, as a script sees them.

An actor is what a world file holds and the editor's outliner shows : a name, a pose, children, tags and components. A ShardActor is a handle to one (a generation and a slot, never a pointer) : it fails with SHARD_E_STALE_HANDLE once the actor is destroyed, and a handle of another actor never takes its place. 0 is never valid.

Where it may be called ("thread : script") : from the callbacks of a script (shard_scripts.h), from on_load / on_play_start... and the other callbacks of the plugin that run on the main thread. NOT from a system (shard_systems.h) : a system runs beside others, and the actors are not made for that (SHARD_E_WRONG_THREAD). A system moves an actor with shard.ecs' set_local_transform.

"In the world of anchor``" : the functions that create or look for actors work in the world the anchor actor is in. A script passes its owner. The engine's components are reached by the name their serialized form carries ("light", "model"...), their fields as JSON text : the format of the world files, so anything the editor shows can be read and set from here.

docs.title: shard_assets.h
docs.text:
Interface "shard.assets" 1.0 : the assets of the project, by path and by id.

An asset is a file of the project the engine knows (its asset database gives it an id : the value of a SHARD_FIELD_ASSET, shard_components.h) under a path in the project ("models/crate.fbx"). shard.content is the other way in : the files a plugin ships in its own folder, as mod:// addresses. A path given here is a path in the project ; a mod:// address is also accepted wherever a file is read.

What a plugin does with it : reads the geometry of the models to bake a navigation mesh or to cut the world into voxels, reads the pixels of an image to pack an atlas, reads and writes the files it owns (a baked navigation mesh, a behaviour tree, a UI document, a voxel chunk) and finds its own asset types' files by extension (shard.extensions' "asset.type" gives the loader ; get_asset gives the resource).

A change to an asset on disk (the user saved it, the importer ran) is the hook "AssetImported" of shard.hooks, with the path as subject.

thread : main, unless a function says otherwise. A plugin that writes the project declares the permission "fs.write:project" in its manifest, one that reads outside its own folder "fs.read:project" (a native plugin is trusted whatever it declares, but the user is told).

Value SHARD_IFACE_ASSETS "shard.assets"

What kind of asset a file is. The engine's own kinds ; a plugin's asset type (shard.extensions) is SHARD_ASSET_PLUGIN, the type name is in ShardAssetInfo::typeName.

Value SHARD_ASSET_UNKNOWN 0u SHARD_ASSET_MESH 1u SHARD_ASSET_TEXTURE 2u SHARD_ASSET_MATERIAL 3u SHARD_ASSET_SHADER 4u SHARD_ASSET_WORLD 5u SHARD_ASSET_SOUND 6u SHARD_ASSET_PREFAB 7u SHARD_ASSET_PLUGIN 8u

docs.title: shard_audio.h
docs.text:
Interface "shard.audio" 1.0 : sounds.

Two ways to make a sound. An actor with an "audio" component (add it with shard.actors' add_component, its clip, volume and 3D settings are fields of the component) is played and paused here. A one shot sound needs no actor : it plays once from a place and removes itself when it ends.

A clip is an asset of the project, named by its path in the project ("sounds/shot.wav"). Volumes are 1 for the clip's own level.

thread : script (shard_actors.h says where that is). SHARD_E_UNSUPPORTED : this host has no audio (an offline tool). A host that runs with no sound device (a server, the tests) accepts every call and plays nothing.

Value SHARD_IFACE_AUDIO "shard.audio"

docs.title: shard_debug.h
docs.text:
Interface "shard.debug" 1.0 : drawing for the developer, in the world, from anywhere : a navigation mesh, the path an agent follows, a field of view, a voxel chunk's bounds, a bone, a network ghost, the node a graph is running.

Unlike the gizmos of shard.editor (which draw in the editor, for the selection), this draws in the game's viewport and in the editor's, from a system, a script or a job. Every call adds a shape to this frame's picture ; a shape with a duration stays that many seconds (real time), with 0 it is drawn for one frame only, so a system that draws what it computes calls the functions again each frame and never clears anything.

The shapes are projected and drawn over the picture by the host's overlay. SHARD_DEBUG_DEPTH_TEST asks that the world's geometry hides them ; a host that cannot do it draws them over everything. Nothing here costs anything in a build that has no debug drawing (a player of a shipped game may turn it off) : the calls are accepted and draw nothing.

Colours are 8 bit r, g, b, a packed as r | g << 8 | b << 16 | a << 24. Positions are in the world ; a large world's are doubles in the rest of the ABI, here floats relative to the camera's region are enough for drawing and the host rebases them.

thread : any. A sandboxed plugin (tier 2) is not offered this interface.

Value SHARD_IFACE_DEBUG "shard.debug" SHARD_DEBUG_DEPTH_TEST 0x01u hidden by the geometry in front of it, where the host can

docs.title: shard_editor.h
docs.text:
Interface "shard.editor" 1.2 : the editor's windows, menus, toolbar, inspectors and gizmos, drawn with a small set of widgets.

ImGui has no stable ABI, so a plugin does not draw with it : it adds a panel and draws the contents with the widgets of ShardUiApi, which the editor implements with its own ImGui. The panel is a window of the editor's Window menu (hidden until the user opens it). Its draw function runs every frame while the window is open, on the editor's main thread, and may call the widgets then and only then. The same widgets draw an inspector (below a component in the Properties panel) ; ShardGizmoApi draws over the viewport.

This interface exists only in the editor : in the player, in headless runs and in the offline tools query_interface answers SHARD_E_NOT_FOUND, so a plugin that has panels keeps working there. The editor loads a plugin whose manifest "hosts" include "engine" (the default) or "editor". A sandboxed plugin (tier 2) needs the permission "editor" in its manifest.

Widgets that take a value change it in place and return SHARD_TRUE on the frame the user changed it. A label may carry a hidden id after "##" ("Speed##enemy1"), as in ImGui, to tell apart two widgets with the same text.

1.1 added to ShardUiApi (from text_disabled on) : more text, vectors, multiline text, groups, children, disabled sections, tabs, tables, menus, popups, item queries, and to ShardEditorApi (from add_menu_item on) : menu items, toolbar buttons, inspectors, gizmos, the selection, notifications.

1.2 added to ShardUiApi (from draw_line on) what a node editor, a timeline or a curve editor needs : a draw list (lines, shapes, Bezier curves, text, clipping) in the window's coordinates, the cursor and mouse queries to build interactions on top of it, hit areas, images, and drag and drop ; and to ShardEditorApi (from undo_push on) : the undo history, opening an asset of a plugin's type with a double click, and the entries of the content browser's "Create" menu. A graph editor (visual scripting, behaviour trees, animation graphs) is made of exactly these.

Interface "shard.experimental.world_ecs" 0.1 : the engine's entities from the main thread, outside the systems.

The interfaces named "shard.experimental.*" are offered so that what may still change can be tried before it is frozen into the ABI. They carry NO compatibility promise : one may change or disappear in any revision of the engine. Their major is 0, and query_interface hands one out only for the exact minor the engine has (query_interface("shard.experimental.world_ecs", 0, 1, ...)) : a plugin built against another one does not get it. A native plugin that carries a valid signature of a trusted publisher (what is distributed) is refused them : every function returns SHARD_E_UNSUPPORTED. Their structs are not pinned by the layout tests.

world_ecs : open() gives a ShardEcs over the engine's registry that every function of shard.ecs (shard_ecs.h) accepts, as an exclusive system would (any type) ; the structural changes are applied by close(). Between the two, the main thread functions of the other interfaces keep working. Open and close in the same callback ; what a plugin leaves open is closed when its context goes.

docs.title: shard_jobs.h
docs.text:
Interface "shard.jobs" 1.0 : the engine's worker threads, for a plugin's own work.

A plugin that bakes a navigation mesh, meshes a chunk of voxels, finds a path, packs a network message or evaluates a pose should not start threads of its own next to the engine's : the engine already has one pool, sized for the machine and shared by the renderer, the physics and the scheduler. These functions run a plugin's work on it.

What a job may call : the functions the headers document as "thread : any" (blobs, shard.time, shard.assets reads, shard.render's mesh and texture creation, shard.debug, shard.events emit...) and the plugin's own code. NOT the ones that say "thread : main", "system" or "script" (actors, ECS, physics, input, editor...) : a job runs beside the frame, and none of those is made for that (SHARD_E_WRONG_THREAD). To get a result back to the main thread, call post_main from the job.

A job that is still running when the plugin is disabled is waited for first : the host never calls a function of a library it is about to unload. A job that never ends therefore blocks the disabling : keep them short, or check a flag of your own.

thread : any, for every function except wait and parallel_for (below). A sandboxed plugin (tier 2) is not offered this interface.

typedef uint64_t ShardJob;    // a job (or a group of them) in flight ; 0 is never valid

One slice [begin, end) of a parallel_for

docs.title: shard_net.h
docs.text:
Interface "shard.net" 1.0 : UDP and TCP sockets, for the networking a game builds itself.

The engine does not impose a protocol, a topology or a replication scheme : a plugin brings the ones its game wants (client/server, lockstep, rollback, a lobby) and this gives it the transport. The sockets are non blocking and driven by the host : it reads and writes them on the frame, and tells the plugin what happened through ONE callback per socket, on the main thread, so a plugin's networking code runs in the same thread as the simulation it feeds and needs no locks. The host polls at the start of every frame ; poll() delivers the events that arrived since, for the plugin that wants to read just before a fixed step.

Reliability, ordering, fragmentation, encryption and NAT traversal are the plugin's: UDP gives datagrams (up to 65507 bytes, no promise), TCP a stream (events carry whatever chunk arrived : frame your messages). Addresses are IPv4. Name resolution happens on a worker, never in the frame.

A plugin that uses it declares the permission "net" in its manifest (a native plugin is trusted whatever it declares, but the user is told ; a sandboxed plugin is not offered this interface). The host caps a plugin at 64 sockets, 1 MiB queued per TCP socket and 256 events a socket per poll (the rest comes with the next poll) ; sockets are closed with the plugin (disable or unload).

To keep two peers' simulations the same, number your messages with the tick of shard.time (fixedStep) and compare shard.time's state_hash.

thread : main, unless a function says otherwise. A sandboxed plugin (tier 2) is not offered this interface.

docs.title: shard_physics.h
docs.text:
Interface "shard.physics" 1.1 : the rigid bodies of actors, ray casts and volume queries, and colliders a plugin builds itself.

A body is the engine's "physics_body" component of an actor (add it with shard.actors' add_component, its shape and mass are fields of the component). These functions move and push the body of an actor : its handle is the actor's. Positions, directions and velocities are in the world, in the units of the project (one unit is one metre unless the project says otherwise), forces in newtons and impulses in newton seconds. Contacts are not asked for here : a script is told about them (on_contact_* in shard_scripts.h).

1.1 added, from raycast_all on : queries that return every hit (rays, overlaps of a sphere, a box and a capsule, sphere and box sweeps) with a filter (layers, an actor to ignore, a tag), and colliders the plugin builds from triangles or boxes (a voxel chunk, a navigation obstacle, a heightfield cut into a mesh) that exist in the physics world without an actor. A hit on one of them reports its collider and userData.

thread : script (shard_actors.h says where that is). SHARD_E_NOT_FOUND : the actor has no physics body, or it has no live body yet. SHARD_E_UNSUPPORTED : this host has no physics (an offline tool).

docs.title: shard_reflect.h
docs.text:
Interface "shard.reflect" 1.0 : what exists in the engine and in the other plugins, described at run time ; and functions plugins offer to be called by name.

A tool that does not know the game when it is written needs this : a visual scripting editor lists the components, their fields, the events and the functions it can wire together, a UI binds a label to "Health.current" of an actor, a console completes names, a network layer walks the fields of a component to send them. The engine's own components ("light", "model"...), the components and scripts of every C plugin, the events described with shard.events' describe and the functions below are all listed through the same calls.

A FUNCTION is a named piece of code with a typed signature : "nav.set_destination(actor, vec3) -> bool". A plugin registers the ones it wants a graph, a UI binding or a console to call ; anything with a signature that fits is called through function_call with ShardValues. They are not a way for plugins to call each other in hot code (shard.services is) : a call converts its arguments to ShardValue and back.

Names live in one flat space. A plugin prefixes its own with its id or a short name of its choice ("nav.set_destination") ; a function another plugin already registered under that name is SHARD_E_ALREADY_EXISTS.

thread : main, except where a function says otherwise.

Value SHARD_IFACE_REFLECT "shard.reflect"

docs.title: shard_render.h
docs.text:
Interface "shard.render" 1.0 : what a plugin puts on the screen that the engine's components do not : meshes it builds, textures it fills, sprites, instances and a 2D overlay.

The engine draws from a snapshot of the simulation (Extract stage), not from the world, and so does this : a plugin hands the renderer RESOURCES (a mesh, a texture, a material), and RETAINED things that use them (a render object, a batch of sprites, an overlay), which the host copies into each frame's snapshot. Nothing here draws "now" : a call records, the frame draws. The GPU work happens on the render thread ; the plugin never waits for it, and a handle can be used at once even if its upload is not done (what is not uploaded yet is not drawn).

- voxels      : a Mesh per chunk (mesh_create from a job), a RenderObject per chunk, a texture array for the atlas
- particles   : a SpriteBatch (sprite_batch_set every frame from a system), or an InstanceBatch of meshes
- animation   : a skinned Mesh (JOINTS + WEIGHTS) and object_set_pose with the bone matrices every frame

  • runtime UI : an Overlay (a callback that draws the UI's geometry into the frame), Geometry and Textures for what it draws, and 

    an Overlay on a render-target Texture to put a UI on a surface of the world

  • navigation, AI, networking : shard.debug draws their debug views

Handles are 64 bit, owned by the plugin, 0 is never valid, and all of them are released with the plugin (disable or unload). Positions in the world are the ABI's usual ones (shard_actors.h) ; a large world's positions are doubles. Matrices are 16 floats, column major (x axis first). Colours are 8 bit r, g, b, a packed as r | g << 8 | b << 16 | a << 24, straight (not premultiplied) alpha.

thread : any, for the functions that create, update or destroy a resource or a retained thing (they take a lock and record). thread : main for load_*, the camera and the overlay's callback. A host without a renderer (a server, a tool, the tests) accepts every call, keeps the handles and draws nothing : SHARD_E_UNSUPPORTED only for the functions that read the screen back (camera_info, world_to_screen...).

docs.title: shard_scripts.h
docs.text:
Interface "shard.scripts" 1.2 : scripts, the components that carry a plugin's gameplay code.

A script is an object of the plugin (a C++ class in the SDK) that lives on an actor, as the engine's own Script components do. The host owns its memory and calls it back : it is created with the component, receives the callbacks of the actor's life and of the frame (play, tick, fixed tick, late tick, stop...), in the order of the scripts of the world, and goes with the actor. Its fields are shown by the inspector, saved with the world and copied with the actor (play mode copies the world), exactly as for a component of shard_components.h : the same ShardFieldDesc, the same field types (text, assets, blobs included), at offsets in the object.

Unlike a component's block, the object is NOT plain data : it is constructed in place in storage the host provides (size bytes, aligned on align), and destructed there. It is never moved or copied by the host with memcpy. A copy of the actor (play mode) constructs a new object and copies the described fields into it : what is not a field starts fresh, as if the actor was just created.

Threads : every callback runs on the thread that ticks the scripts of the world, one script after the other, never two at once : what a script does with shard_actors.h and shard_input.h is safe there. The functions of this table are "thread : main" (from on_load).

Edit mode (1.2) : the engine ticks scripts only while the world plays (on_create does run when a script joins an actor in the editor, on_play only in play mode). A script that has to be seen working while it is being made -- a particle emitter, a UI being laid out, an animation being scrubbed, a navigation mesh being tuned -- sets SHARD_SCRIPT_EDIT_MODE in its description : on_edit_tick is then called every frame the world does NOT play (with the real frame time). on_field_changed is called when the inspector edits one of a script's fields, in either mode. What a script does in edit mode must not change what gets saved: the world file holds the fields, not the state of an effect.

Value SHARD_IFACE_SCRIPTS "shard.scripts" SHARD_SCRIPT_MAX_SIZE 16384u bytes of an object

The callbacks of a script. All are optional but construct and destruct. A callback returns SHARD_OK, or an error that the host logs and counts as an error of the plugin (at the tenth the host fails the plugin, as for a system). object is what construct built.

docs.title: shard_time.h
docs.text:
Interface "shard.time" 1.0 : the simulation's clock, and a fingerprint of its state.

A system or a script is handed the step it runs for (shard_systems.h, shard_scripts.h) ; this is for the rest : a particle emitter that wants the simulation time to seed its randomness, a network layer that numbers its ticks, a UI that animates in real time.

Two kinds of time. The simulation's (simTime, fixedStep) advances by whole fixed steps and only while the world plays : a replay of the run reproduces it exactly, so anything that changes what the game looks like must use it. The wall clock (realTime) is the machine's : for what is not part of the simulation (a loading spinner, a cursor blink, a network time-out) and never for what the game decides. The time_scale of the engine (slow motion, pause) acts on the first and not on the second.

thread : any, except the setters (main).

docs.title: shard_wasm.h
docs.text:
Sandboxed plugins (tier 2, "abi": "wasm1") : the C ABI, for a module built for wasm32 (docs/design-notes/wasm-sandbox.fr.md). Experimental : it is not covered by the ABI's compatibility promise yet.

A sandboxed plugin is the plugin you would write for the C ABI (shard.h, or shard/game.hpp in C++), compiled to WebAssembly. It can touch nothing but its own memory and what the host gives it : no files, no network, no clock, no randomness of the system. It loads without a signature or a consent, because it cannot do more than the host lets it : the interfaces below, filtered by the "permissions" of its manifest. Its time (budgets.frameMs per frame) and its memory (budgets.memoryMB) are bounded ; a trap (a division by zero, an access out of its memory, an unreachable), an exhausted budget or an import used wrongly stops the plugin, never the engine.

The same source compiles for the engine and for wasm32. This header is all it takes : including it (shard.h does, when compiling for wasm) declares every function of the interfaces as an import of the host and builds the tables (ShardCVarsApi...) from them. The ShardHostApi that shard_plugin_entry receives is shard_wasm_host_table, which the module exports ; query_interface answers from the module's tables. See shard_wasm_imports.h (generated from the other headers) for the list.

What differs from a native plugin :

  • the interfaces : shard.plugin, commands, cvars, components, ecs, systems, events, state, scripts, actors, input, physics, audio, worlds, 

    and shard.content for the plugin's own folder ("fs.read:content"). Not offered : shard.editor, hooks, services, extensions, experimental.

  • permissions : shard.content needs "fs.read:content", shard.input "input", shard.physics "physics", shard.audio "audio" (without it 

    query_interface says SHARD_E_NOT_FOUND and the functions answer SHARD_E_UNSUPPORTED, or SHARD_FALSE / 0), worlds.load_world
"worlds.load", actors.create / actors.spawn / worlds.spawn_prefab "actors.spawn".

  • memory of the host is copied : the block of a component that shard.ecs hands out, the bytes of a blob and the object of a script 

    live in the module, and what the module changed is copied back when the call that made the copy returns (a system, a script's
callback, a command...). A blob's pointer stays valid until the module resizes or frees the blob. A string the host hands out
(shard.components string_get) is valid until the call returns.

  • the systems of a module run on the main thread, one after the other : a module is never entered by two threads at once.

  • ShardPluginCtx : whatever a module passes, an import acts for the plugin the module belongs to.

  • shard.content.read gives memory that is freed with ShardHostApi::free ; resolve and resolve_logical (which would give a path of the 

    host) are always SHARD_E_UNSUPPORTED, and read / list only reach the plugin's own mod:// address.

  • the host's alloc and free are the module's memory (they count against budgets.memoryMB).

Building one, in C without a libc :

clang --target=wasm32 -ffreestanding -nostdlib -O2 -I<sdk>/include -c plugin.c -o plugin.o
wasm-ld --no-entry --export=shard_plugin_entry --export=shard_wasm_host_table --export-table -o plugin.wasm plugin.o

... and in C++ with wasi-sdk (a libc and a libc++ for wasm32, no exceptions) :

clang++ --target=wasm32-wasi -fno-exceptions -DSHARD_SDK_NO_EXCEPTIONS -O2 -I<sdk>/include -c a.cpp b.cpp
wasm-ld ... or clang++ -mexec-model=reactor -Wl,--export=shard_plugin_entry -Wl,--export=shard_wasm_host_table -Wl,--export-table

shard_sdk_add_plugin(... TARGET wasm) does that (sdk/cmake/ShardSDKPlugin.cmake). The module must export its memory ("memory", wasm-ld's default) and its function table ("__indirect_function_table", --export-table) : the host reads the arguments of the imports in the first and calls the callbacks through the second. A module with C++ constructors (or a libc to start) exports _initialize (wasi-sdk reactors do) or __wasm_call_ctors : the host runs it before the entry point. The module's allocator must get its memory from memory.grow, as wasi-libc's does : the host adds pages of its own after the module's.

docs.text:
Interface "shard.worlds" 1.1 : loading worlds, and prefabs ; and which worlds are loaded (1.1).

A world is loaded by its path in the project ("worlds/arena.world"). The load is a request : it starts in the background, and the world is swapped in at the start of a following frame, where the old worlds are unloaded (their scripts get on_destroyed) and the new one is loaded (the plugin's on_world_loaded is called). A script that asks for a load keeps running until then, so nothing it holds is pulled from under it in the middle of a frame.

A prefab is an actor stored as JSON in the content of a module (prefabs/<name>.json, shard_content.h) : the form the editor writes an actor in. Spawning one builds the actor, its components and its children.

docs.title: The C++ SDK
docs.text: sdk/include/shard/cpp : header-only C++17 over the C ABI, compiled into the plugin. #include <shard/cpp/plugin.hpp> brings all of it. Every callback of the SDK catches what the plugin throws : Shard::Error (what a registration the host refused throws, with its ShardResult) and anything else become an error of that callback, with the message in the log. Below, the public declarations of each header (bodies left out).

docs.title: shard/cpp/plugin.hpp
docs.text:
Shard C++ SDK : a plugin class over the C ABI.

class SpinPlugin : public Shard::Plugin {
public:
    void OnLoad(Shard::Context& ctx) override { ... }
};
SHARD_C_PLUGIN(SpinPlugin)

The macro exports shard_plugin_entry and fills the callbacks table : every callback catches what the plugin throws (Shard::Error from a refused registration, or anything else) and turns it into an error the host fails the plugin with, the message in its log. Nothing of the engine is included or linked : this compiles against sdk/include alone, with any C++17 compiler.

struct Spin { float speed = 1.f; float angle = 0.f; Shard::Vec3 axis{ 0.f, 1.f, 0.f }; };

docs.text:
What a plugin is told about the actor components of a type (ABI 1.4 of shard.components) : block is the component's values, on the main thread, in the editor's edit mode as well as in play mode.

Shard C++ SDK : services between plugins (shard_services.h). A service is a C table of function pointers that starts with uint32_t structSize, published in a header by its provider :

struct WeatherApi { uint32_t structSize; float (SHARD_CALL *rain)(void* self, float x, float z); };
ctx.Services().Provide("weather.query", 1, 0, &kWeatherApi, this);                 // the provider
auto weather = ctx.Services().Get<WeatherApi>("weather.query", "^1");              // a user, in OnInitialize
if (auto w = weather.Resolve()) w.table->rain(w.self, 0.f, 0.f);                   // before each use

docs.text:
Shard C++ SDK : windows of the editor (shard_editor.h).

SHARD_EDITOR_PANEL(Spawner, "Enemy spawner", ui)
{
    static int count = 5;
    ui.SliderInt("Count", count, 1, 50);
    if (ui.Button("Spawn")) SpawnEnemies(count);
}

The panel appears in the editor's Window menu. Menu items (SHARD_EDITOR_MENU_ITEM), toolbar buttons, inspectors below a component, gizmos in the viewport and the selection are in the same header. In the player, in headless runs and in the offline tools there is no editor : the panel is not added and nothing else changes, so the same plugin runs everywhere. A plugin whose manifest hosts include "engine" is loaded by the editor ; "editor" alone limits it to the editor.

docs.title: shard/cpp/engine_components.hpp
docs.text:
Shard C++ SDK : the engine's own components (model, light, physics body...) as typed handles, over shard.actors' field functions.

Shard::Actor bullet = GetScene().Create("Bullet");

auto model = bullet.Add<Shard::Model>();
model.SetMesh(mesh);                                       // an AssetId (a field of the script), or the asset's name in the project
model.SetMaterial(0, material);

auto body = bullet.Add<Shard::PhysicsBody>();
body.SetShape(Shard::Shape::Capsule(0.1f, 0.3f));
body.SetMotionType(Shard::MotionType::Dynamic);            // the body of the new kind exists at once : the velocity has something to push
body.SetFriction(0.8f);
bullet.SetVelocity(forward * 30.f);

if (auto light = bullet.Get<Shard::Light>()) light.SetIntensity(3.f);

A handle is a pair (actor, component type) : copying it is free, and it stays safe when the actor goes. Every setter changes that one field and nothing else, the way an edit in the inspector does (the component's own change hook runs : a body keeps its velocity when its friction changes) and throws Shard::Error when the engine refuses it. The getters return a zero when the component or the field is gone.

Not every component has a class here : Shard::ComponentRef reaches any field of any component of the engine by its name (the one the inspector and the world file use) :

Shard::ComponentRef probe(actor, "probeVolume");
probe.SetFloat("blendDistance", 2.f);

Assets read as their name in the project (the way a world file stores them) and are set from an AssetId or from that name.

docs.title: shard/cpp/field.hpp
docs.text:
Shard C++ SDK : the fields of a script, declared where the member is.

class Gun : public Shard::Script {
public:
    SHARD_FIELD(float, power, Range(0.f, 1000.f), Tooltip("Speed of the bullet")) = 30.f;
    SHARD_FIELD(float, lifetime, Range(0.f, 60.f)) = 3.f;
    SHARD_FIELD(Shard::AssetId, mesh, Tooltip("The mesh to shoot"));
    SHARD_FIELD(int, ammo, Runtime()) = 12;                  // shown by the inspector, not saved
    float cooldown = 0.f;                                    // not a field : it stays out of the inspector and the world file
};

// gun.cpp
SHARD_REGISTER_SCRIPT(Gun)

The macro declares the member (Type name, so the default value goes after it, as for any member) and, in front of it, a one byte member that tells the SDK its name, its type, where it is in the object and its options. Nothing else lists the field : no sequence in the .cpp, no generated file. Options are the names below, written bare inside the macro:

Range(min, max)     the bounds of the inspector's widget
Tooltip("text")     what the inspector shows when the mouse rests on the field
Runtime()           the inspector shows it, read only, and the world file does not save it
Hidden()            neither shown nor saved (the object keeps it; not for a string)

The type is any of the field types of shard/cpp/component.hpp (numbers, bool, Vec2/3/4, Quat, Color, Text, AssetId, std::string, Actor, Blob).

docs.title: shard/cpp/jobs.hpp
docs.text:
Shard C++ SDK : the engine's worker threads (shard_jobs.h).

// bake something off the frame, then hand the result to the simulation
auto job = Shard::Jobs::Run([chunk](uint32_t /*worker*/) { chunk->BuildMesh(); });
...
job.Wait();                                           // or let it go: ~JobHandle releases it, the work still runs to its end

Shard::Jobs::ParallelFor(agents.size(), [&](uint32_t i, uint32_t /*worker*/) { agents[i].Steer(dt); });     // returns when all are done
Shard::Jobs::PostMain([] { /* back on the main thread, at the start of the next frame */ });

A job may call what the headers document as "thread : any" (blobs, shard.render's resources, shard.debug, the maths...) and the plugin's own code, not the actors, the ECS, the physics or the input (they are made for the thread of the simulation). A job that is still running when the plugin is disabled is waited for first.

docs.text:
A job (or the slices of a ParallelForAsync) in flight. Move only ; letting go of it does not stop the work.

JobHandle& operator=(JobHandle&& other) noexcept;
JobHandle& operator=(const JobHandle&) = delete;

docs.title: Jobs
docs.text:
/// The threads that work for the engine, the calling one included : the size of a per-worker scratch array
static uint32_t WorkerCount();
/// Runs `fn(worker)` on a worker. Keep the handle to Wait for it ; drop it to let the job go on its own.
template <typename F> static JobHandle Run(F&& fn);
/// The same, without a handle : nothing will wait for it
template <typename F> static void RunDetached(F&& fn);
/// Calls `fn(index, worker)` for every index of [0, count), on every worker at once, and returns when all are done. The order is not defined :
/// write to a slot per index, combine in index order. `grain` : how many indices a slice has (0 : the host picks).
template <typename F> static void ParallelFor(uint32_t count, F&& fn, uint32_t grain = 0);
/// `fn(begin, end, worker)` on slices of [0, count) : for a body with a setup per slice
template <typename F> static void ParallelForRange(uint32_t count, F&& fn, uint32_t grain = 0);
/// The same, without waiting : the closure is kept until the last slice ended
template <typename F> static JobHandle ParallelForAsync(uint32_t count, F&& fn, uint32_t grain = 0);
/// Runs `fn()` on the main thread at the start of the next frame : how a job hands its result to the simulation. thread : any
template <typename F> static void PostMain(F&& fn);

Shard C++ SDK : UDP and TCP sockets, for the networking a game builds itself (shard_net.h).

// a server : datagrams on a port
Shard::Net::UdpSocket server = Shard::Net::OpenUdp(27015, [&](const Shard::Net::Event& e) {
    if (e.kind == Shard::Net::EventKind::Data) HandleDatagram(e.peer, e.data, e.size);
});
server.SendTo({ "192.0.2.7", 27016 }, bytes.data(), bytes.size());

// a client : a stream
Shard::Net::TcpSocket client = Shard::Net::Connect({ "example.com", 4000 }, [&](const Shard::Net::Event& e) { ... });

The events arrive on the main thread, at the start of the frame (Net::Poll() reads just before a fixed step). The plugin declares the permission "net" in its manifest. The sockets close with the object, and with the plugin.

docs.text:
Shard C++ SDK : random numbers that a replay of the run reproduces (shard_plugin.h, random_stream).

class Kicker : public Shard::Script {
    void OnPlay() override { m_Random = Shard::Random::Stream("Kicker/" + Owner().Name()); }
    void OnTick(float) override { Owner().AddImpulse(m_Random.OnUnitSphere() * 4.f); }
    Shard::Random m_Random;
};

rand(), std::random_device and std::uniform_*_distribution give different numbers from one run, platform or standard library to the next, so a replay or a networked simulation that used them would drift. A stream starts from the run's seed, and this class (PCG32, the generator of the engine's own Core::Random) produces the same numbers everywhere. Not for cryptography.

docs.title: shard/cpp/registry.hpp
docs.text:
Shard C++ SDK : registrations that live where the code lives.

A plugin of one file registers everything in OnLoad. A game does not: each .cpp defines its own scripts, components and systems and says so at the bottom of the file, with one of these macros. They add themselves to a list when the library is loaded, and the SDK runs the list at the start of OnLoad, in a fixed order (by kind, then by name - never by the order the compiler happened to link the files, which would change the ids of the components and the order of the systems from one build to the next).

SHARD_REGISTER_SCRIPT(Health, (maxHealth)(current))                   // shard/cpp/script.hpp
SHARD_DEFINE_COMPONENT(Velocity, (x)(y)(z))                           // a component of plain data, found anywhere with Shard::ComponentOf<Velocity>()
SHARD_ON_LOAD(Movement, ctx) { ctx.Systems().Add(...).Run(...); }     // anything else: systems, cvars, commands, hooks, events...

The macros go at global scope, in a source file of the plugin's library (not in a static library the plugin links: the linker may drop a file nothing references).

/// The body that follows runs in OnLoad, after the components and the scripts are registered: `ctx` is the Shard::Context. `Name` only orders
/// and names it (unique in the plugin, letters and digits).
SHARD_ON_LOAD(Name, ctx)

docs.title: shard/cpp/script.hpp
docs.text:
Shard C++ SDK : scripts, the gameplay classes of a game (shard_scripts.h).

// health.hpp
class Health : public Shard::Script {
public:
    float maxHealth = 100.f;                    // fields: shown in the inspector, saved with the world
    float current = 100.f;
    Shard::Text label;

    void OnPlay() override { current = maxHealth; }
    void OnTick(float dt) override { if (current <= 0.f) Owner().Destroy(); }
    void Damage(float amount) { current -= amount; }
};

// health.cpp
#include "health.hpp"
SHARD_REGISTER_SCRIPT(Health, (maxHealth)(current)(label))

Put as many scripts as you like in as many files as you like: each registers itself (shard/cpp/registry.hpp). In the editor the script is a component, "<plugin id>.Health", that you add to an actor like any other: its object is created with the component, its callbacks run in play mode in the same order as the engine's own scripts (the order the components were added), and it goes with the actor.

The class is a normal C++ class: any member that is not listed stays out of the inspector and the world file, and starts fresh (a copy of the actor for play mode builds a new object and copies the listed fields into it). Keep the constructor free of calls into the engine (the SDK builds one to learn where the fields are): do that work in OnCreate or OnPlay.

/// Every frame the world does NOT play (the editor's edit mode), with the real frame time : a particle emitter, a UI being laid out, a preview.
/// Only for a class that declares `static constexpr bool kExecuteInEditMode = true;`. What it does must not change what gets saved.
virtual void OnEditTick(float /*deltaTime*/);
/// The inspector (or an undo, or SetComponentJson) edited a field : its index among the fields the class registered, in the order of the
/// registration (Shard::FieldIndex<T>("name") finds an index by name). Not called for what the script changes itself.
virtual void OnFieldChanged(uint32_t /*fieldIndex*/);

const Actor& Owner() const;

/// The index of the field `name` of the script class T (what OnFieldChanged is told), or -1
template <typename T> int FieldIndex(const std::string& name);

/// Registers the class T as "<plugin id>.<name>" (from OnLoad: SHARD_REGISTER_SCRIPT does it). Throws Shard::Error if the host refuses it.

/// Registers a script class under its class name. At global scope, in a source file of the plugin (it needs <shard/game.hpp>).
/// The fields are the members the class declares with SHARD_FIELD (shard/cpp/field.hpp), each with its own options, in the header :

docs.title: shard/cpp/time.hpp
docs.text:
Shard C++ SDK : the simulation's clock and a fingerprint of its state (shard_time.h).

const auto t = Shard::Time::Now();
Send(Message{ t.fixedStep, ... });                    // a tick number two peers agree on
if (t.fixedStep % 60 == 0) Send(Shard::Time::Hash()); // compare it with the other peer's to know they stayed in step

simTime and fixedStep are the simulation's (a replay reproduces them) ; realTime is the machine's, for what is not part of the game.

docs.title: SDK headers
docs.text:
sdk/include/shard/*.h is the C ABI : plugins built by other people, with other compilers, against an older revision, call these structs and tables. Changes there are reviewed for compatibility first :

  • only additions inside a major revision : a function at the end of a table, a field at the end of a struct, a new interface. Never reorder, resize or remove ;
  • every addition raises SHARD_ABI_MINOR, the interface's minor in query_interface and sdk/VERSION, and goes into the table of revisions of sdk/README.md ;
  • tests/plugins/abi_layout_tests.cpp is updated in the same change, deliberately : when it fails, a layout moved ;
  • tests/plugin_fixtures/abi_1_0 is never edited : the plugin built against it has to keep loading.

What is not ready to be frozen goes into a shard.experimental.* interface (shard_experimental.h) : major 0, no promise, refused to signed native plugins, not pinned, not counted in SHARD_ABI_MINOR. Moving it to a frozen interface later is an ordinary addition.

The comments of these headers are the API reference : scripts/gen_api_reference.py (or the ShardApiReference target) writes the page from them, and the test Docs.ApiReference fails when the committed page is not what the headers give, or when a header announces another revision than the one the engine offers. Write the comments for the reader of that page : the first comment of an interface's header starts with Interface "shard.x" M.m : what it is, a comment just before a struct describes it, ---- Title ---- makes a heading, and backticks are kept as they are.

The C++ SDK (sdk/include/shard/cpp) is compiled into each plugin : it can change freely, as long as it only uses the C ABI.

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text: Build the engine, open the example project in the editor, and run the tests.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• CMake 3.28.2 or later.
  • A C++17 compiler : GCC or Clang on Linux (with make or ninja), GCC MinGW recommended on Windows.
  • git, to clone the submodules.
git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/Windokk/Shard.git
cd Shard
# already cloned without them ?  git submodule update --init --recursive

docs.title: The editor's fonts
docs.text:
Place these two fonts in resources/editor_resources/fonts/ (on both platforms) :

  • OpenSans-Regular.ttf
  • lucide.ttf

docs.title: Build and run
docs.text:
LinuxWindows

Install what SDL3 needs to build its X11 / Wayland / audio / input backends, plus zlib and liburing (optional, faster async IO) :

bash scripts/install_linux_deps.sh        # Debian / Ubuntu

On another distribution install the equivalent packages : see the SDL3 Linux notes.

./build.sh              # add Release for an optimized build
SHARD_NO_RUN=1 ./build.sh   # build only, do not start the editor

build.sh makes imgui use the engine's vulkan.h, configures, builds everything and starts the editor on the example project.

From Git Bash or MSYS2, make the imgui submodule use the engine's vulkan.h :

bash scripts/patch_imgui.sh

Then run build.bat (or build.sh). It compiles everything from the root : submodules, the engine, the editor and the game module. SDL3.dll is built with the project and lands in the build folder.

Copy the resources/engine_resources and resources/editor_resources folders inside the build directory.

To start the editor by hand on the example project, with OpenGL core as the rendering API :

./ShardEditor.exe --game plugins/game/bin/windows-x86_64/libGameModule.dll --project ../example_project/example_project.json --api opengl

The reflection files (*.reflection.hpp) are committed : ShardReflect only has to be run, with scripts/regen_reflection.sh, after changing a reflected class.

docs.title: Run the tests
docs.text:
The tests are built with the project :

ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure

On Linux, bash scripts/smoke_test.sh (after a build) starts the player on the example project, loads its Cornell box world, renders a few frames and shuts down : it fails on a crash, a hang or an error in the log.

docs.title: No window, no GPU
docs.text:
ShardHeadless runs the simulation with no window, GPU or sound card, and can play back a recorded run and check that the state is the same on every frame :

ShardHeadless --game <module> --project <project.json> --replay run.replay

See Headless mode and determinism.

docs.title: Display: linear lighting, tonemapping and sRGB
docs.text:
Lighting is computed in linear space, but monitors expect sRGB and can't go brighter than white. The engine therefore renders in linear HDR and converts only at the very end, in two places:

sRGB textures --(decoded by the GPU when sampled)--> linear HDR scene --(tonemap pass)--> 8-bit sRGB image

docs.title: Pipeline
docs.text:
Stage Details Color textures (albedo, diffuse, emissive, basecolor slots) Stored as sRGB (GL_SRGB8_ALPHA8, BC7 sRGB). The GPU converts them to linear when sampling and filters in linear space. Data textures (normal, metallic, roughness, AO) stay linear. The slot type comes from the sampler name (IsColorTextureSlot). Mipmaps of color textures are built in linear space, so a distant checkerboard averages to the right grey. Sky Radiance .hdr files are loaded as RGB16F floats, which keeps the sun far brighter than the sky. 8-bit skies and 6-face cubemaps are decoded from sRGB. The irradiance and prefilter convolutions clamp samples to 500, otherwise the sun disc overflows 16-bit floats and the diffuse term flickers. Scene The forward pass renders into a multisampled RGBA16F target, so values above 1 are kept. Tonemap (shaders/fb/tonemap.frag) Resolves the scene, applies exposure, the tonemapper and the sRGB curve, adds a little dithering against banding in skies and soft shadows, and writes the 8-bit viewport. Overlays Grid, outlines, billboards and debug shapes are drawn after tonemapping with their colors unchanged. They depth-test against a copy of the scene depth.

Renderer::GetViewportTextureHandle still returns the final image, used by the editor, --screenshot and the player.

Thumbnails and material previews render straight to an 8-bit target, so lit.frag converts the color itself in that case (outputDisplayColors, ACES, no exposure).

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
Found in World Settings > Display. They are written under display in the world file when they differ from the defaults.

Setting Tonemapper aces (default, filmic), neutral (Khronos PBR Neutral: leaves colors below ~0.8 alone and only compresses highlights), reinhard, or none (clamps, so anything above white is white). Exposure (EV) Applied before the curve. +1 doubles the light, -1 halves it.

Debug views treat this differently. Lit goes through the full transform. Unlit and No lighting show albedo and only get the sRGB curve. Normals, depth, UVs, AO and wireframe show raw values.

docs.title: Offline renders and bakes
docs.text: raytrace.render writes linear radiance to an .hdr file, and a .png preview that uses the world's exposure, tonemapper and sRGB curve so it matches the viewport. Baked lightmaps and probes store linear values and go through the same tonemap pass as everything else.

docs.title: Keeping C++ and GLSL in sync
docs.text: rhi/display_transform.hpp is a C++ copy of shaders/common/tonemap.glsl, with the same constants and formulas. It is used for the preview and the tests. Change one, change the other.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• A scene that was lit when everything was clamped will look different. Shadows are brighter (no crushed blacks) and highlights roll off instead of clipping. Adjust Exposure first, then light intensities.
  • Custom shaders that write to the scene target must output linear values, with no gamma applied.
  • A color texture only counts as color if its slot name starts with albedo, diffuse, emissive or basecolor. Any other name is treated as linear data.

docs.title: Event system
docs.text:
How parts of the engine and of a game tell each other that something happened, without knowing each other.

The Events::EventDispatcher (engine/world/event_system.hpp) is a typed publish / subscribe bus, reached with Core::GetEngine().GetEventDispatcher(). An event is a plain struct deriving from Events::Event ; a subscriber receives exactly the type it subscribed to.

docs.title: Scopes
docs.text:
An event is emitted to one scope, and only the subscribers of that scope hear it :

Scope Subscribe Emit Heard by Global subscribeGlobal<T>(cb) emitGlobal(e) everything listening to the type World subscribeToWorld<T>(worldID, cb) emitToWorld(worldID, e) the listeners of one world Actor subscribeToActor<T>(actorID, cb) emitToActor(actorID, e) the listeners of one actor Component subscribeToComponent<T>(componentID, cb) emitToComponent(componentID, e) the listeners of one component

Scopes do not cascade : an event emitted to an actor is not also sent to its world or to the global listeners. Emit it twice if both should hear it.

docs.title: Using it
docs.text:
auto* events = Core::GetEngine().GetEventDispatcher();

// Listen
events->subscribeGlobal<Events::WorldStructureChangedEvent>(
    [](const Events::WorldStructureChangedEvent& e) {
        if (e.changeType == Events::LOADED)
            OnWorldLoaded();
    });

// Send
events->emitGlobal(Events::WorldStructureChangedEvent(worldAssetID, Events::CREATED, "Door", sourceID));

docs.title: Writing your own event
docs.text:
Derive from Event, which carries the sourceObjectID of whoever sent it :

struct DoorOpenedEvent : public Events::Event {
    float openAmount;
    DoorOpenedEvent(float amount, Core::ObjectID source) : Event(source), openAmount(amount) {}
};

Subscribers are found by the exact C++ type (typeid), so an event deriving from another is not delivered to the listeners of its base.

docs.title: Rules to know
docs.text:
• Synchronous. emit calls every handler, in subscription order, before it returns. There is no queue : a slow handler slows the sender, and a handler that emits runs the nested handlers inside itself.
  • No unsubscribe. A subscription lives as long as the dispatcher. A handler that captures this must not outlive the object : subscribe from something that lives for the whole run (the editor's main window does), or check your own state in the handler.
  • Not thread-safe. Subscribe and emit from the main thread, outside parallel systems.
  • Don't change the subscriptions of a type while it is being emitted (subscribing in a handler of the same event), the handler list may move.
  • The event is passed by const& and only valid during the call : copy what you need.

docs.title: Events the engine emits
